transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… the main reason I came in is that I’ve started planning my whole day around avoiding certain roads—specifically those high bridges. Like, I’ll look up routes ahead of time and take the long way just so I don’t have to drive over them. And if there’s no way around it, I can do it, but it’s awful. I’m gripping the wheel the whole time, tense the entire way across, just trying to get through it. It’s gotten to the point where it feels like it’s running more of my day than it should.
Is it the height of the bridges themselves that bothers you, or is it more about driving on them?

It’s… I guess it’s more the height and being up over the water, but it hits me through the driving, if that makes sense. Like, I know those bridges over the bay are built solid. I know thousands of people drive over them every day and nothing happens. I can tell myself that.

But when I’m coming up on one, my mind just goes straight to this picture of the car somehow going over the side. Not that I really believe the bridge is unsafe, exactly, it’s just this awful feeling like there’s nothing between me and that drop, and I’m the one having to keep the car steady. So it’s not regular driving that bothers me—it’s driving on those high bridges.
Do you experience a similar feeling of fear or anxiety when you're in other high places, like tall buildings or mountain edges, or is it primarily just the driving on high bridges that bothers you?

It’s mostly the bridges, especially the high ones over the bay. I mean, I can be aware of height in other places, sure, but what really sets me off is when I’m in the car and I’m the one driving across. I know, logically, those bridges are built fine. People drive over them all day, every day, and nothing happens.

But when I get close to one, it’s like my head stops caring about all that. It starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side, like one wrong move and that’s it. I can tell myself, “This is safe, the bridge is solid,” but my body doesn’t seem to believe it once I’m up there.
Do you feel anxious when you're a passenger in a car driving over a high bridge, or is the fear mostly when you're the one driving?

It’s mostly when I’m driving, I’d say. Being a passenger over one of those high bridges isn’t exactly pleasant either, but the worst part is when I’m the one behind the wheel, because then it feels like it’s on me to keep the car steady.

And I know that probably sounds a little irrational, because I do know those bridges over the bay are built fine. I mean, people drive over them all day, every day, and nothing happens. I know that in my head. But when I get near one, it’s like my mind just doesn’t stay with that. It goes straight to this thought, or almost like a picture, that the car could somehow go right over the side. So even if I’m telling myself, “You’re safe, just keep driving,” my body reacts like there’s real danger right there.
Do you experience similar anxiety when operating other vehicles or machinery that require precision or control, such as a boat or an airplane?

Not really with other things, no. I mean, I don’t fly planes or anything like that, and I’m not out operating heavy machinery. It’s really tied to those bridges over the bay and being in the car up there.

The strange part is, I can sit here and tell you I know those bridges are built fine. I know people drive them every day, all day long, and it’s not like cars are just going over the edge. But when I get near one, it’s like my mind doesn’t go with what I know. It just jumps to this picture that the car could somehow go right over the side. And because I’m the one driving, it feels like every little movement matters too much, even though I know that’s not really how it works.
Does the anxiety you experience when driving over high bridges ever occur in situations where you're not driving, but still have some form of control over your movement or environment?

Not that I’ve really noticed, no. It seems pretty tied to the car and the bridge for me. Like, if I’m walking somewhere or just moving around on my own, I don’t get that same thing in the same way.

It’s really when I’m getting near one of those high bridges over the bay, especially in the car, that my mind starts doing that. I know the bridges are built fine, and I know people drive over them every single day without anything happening. I can say that out loud and believe it sitting here. But once I’m near it, my head starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side, even though I know that doesn’t make sense. That’s the situation where it really grabs me.
Does the fear of going over the side occur when you're a pedestrian on a high bridge?

I don’t really have it that way as a pedestrian, at least not that I can clearly point to. The fear I keep talking about is much more tied to being in the car near those high bridges over the bay.

I mean, I know those bridges are built fine. I know people drive over them all day, every day, and nothing happens. But when I’m coming up on one in the car, my mind just sort of flips into this idea that the car could somehow go right over the side. That’s the picture that gets stuck in my head. Walking on a bridge isn’t really the situation that brings it on like that for me.
Do you experience a similar fear when you are a passenger on a bus or train that crosses over a high bridge?

I guess I’d say it’s closest when I’m in a car. A bus or a train isn’t really the main thing I think of with it. What happens for me is more when I’m coming up on one of those bridges over the bay and I’m in the car, especially if I’m the one driving.

And I know, sitting here, those bridges are built fine. I know people go over them every day, all day long, and nothing happens. But when I get near one, my mind kind of takes off on its own and starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side. It’s not really a sensible thought, but it feels real in that moment.
Does your fear of going over the side ever occur when you're in control of a vehicle or situation other than driving a car over a high bridge?

Not really in any other situation that I can think of. It’s pretty specific for me — it’s those high bridges over the bay, and being in the car.

I mean, I can sit here and tell you I know the bridges are built fine. I know people drive over them every day, all day long, and they’re okay. But when I get close to one, my mind just starts acting like the car could go right over the side. It’s not like I’m having that same thought when I’m controlling some other machine or in some other place. It’s really that car-on-the-bridge situation that gets me.
Is your fear of driving over high bridges ever triggered by just thinking about driving over one, even when you're not actually in a car?

Thinking about it can make me uneasy, but the real thing — the part where it really hits me — is when I actually see the bridge coming up. Like, if I’m in the car and I can see it ahead, that’s when my body reacts right away.

My chest gets tight pretty much as soon as I notice it, and my hands start sweating on the steering wheel. Then I get this kind of tunnel focus where I’m just staring straight ahead, like, “Just keep going, just get to the other side.” I’m not really thinking normally at that point. It’s like I’m locked onto the road and trying to get across without looking around too much.
Is your fear of driving over high bridges lessened at all if someone else is driving you over the bridge, but you're still in the car?

A little, maybe, but it doesn’t really go away. If someone else is driving, I’m not having to hold the wheel, so in that sense I can kind of tell myself, “Just sit here, let them drive.” But once we get near one of those bridges over the bay, my mind still starts doing that same thing.

I know the bridge is built fine. I know people drive over it all day long and nothing happens. I can say that logically. But when we’re actually close to it, even as a passenger, I still get that thought like the car could somehow go right over the side. It’s not as much about who’s driving as it is being in the car on that high bridge.
Is your fear of high bridges ever present when you're not in a vehicle at all, such as when you're at home or in a completely different setting?

No, not really like that. If I’m at home or just somewhere else, I don’t walk around feeling scared of high bridges out of nowhere. I can think about them and know, you know, those bridges over the bay are built fine — people drive them every day, back and forth, all day long. I understand that.

It’s when I’m actually getting near one, in the car, that my mind starts doing that thing where it acts like the car could go right over the side. That’s the part that feels real to me in the moment. Away from the car and away from the bridge, it’s more just a thought, not the same fear.
Does your fear of going over the side occur when you are on a bicycle or motorcycle crossing over a high bridge?

I don’t really ride a motorcycle, and I’m not usually on a bicycle over those kinds of bridges, so I can’t say from experience the same way. For me it’s mostly tied to being in the car and coming up on one of those high bridges over the bay.

Like I’ve said, I know in my head they’re built fine, and I know people drive over them all day, every day. But when I get near one, my mind just starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side. That’s the image or fear that pops in. It’s really the car-on-the-bridge situation that does it for me.
Is your fear of high bridges ever present when you're walking or standing on a bridge, not just driving over it?

I can’t really say it comes up the same way just standing or walking on a bridge. For me, the thing that really sets it off is being in the car and getting near one of those high bridges over the bay.

I know, sitting here talking about it, that those bridges are built fine. I know folks drive over them every single day and nothing happens. But when I’m actually approaching one in a car, my mind starts going to that place where it feels like the car could somehow go right over the side. That’s the part that grabs me. Walking or standing there isn’t really the main thing I’ve noticed—it’s the car being up there on the bridge.
Is your fear of high bridges ever triggered by anything else besides driving over them?

Not really, no. I mean, I can think about high bridges when I’m not on one, but it doesn’t hit me the same way. The thing that seems to set it off is driving toward one of those big bridges over the bay.

It’s strange because I know they’re built right. I know people drive over them every day, all day long, and nothing happens. I can tell myself that sitting here. But once I’m getting near it in the car, my mind starts acting like the car could go right over the side, even though I know that doesn’t make sense. So it’s not really other things triggering it — it’s that situation of being in the car and approaching the bridge.
Is your fear of high bridges ever present when you're a passenger in a vehicle other than a car, such as a truck or an RV, crossing over a high bridge?

I haven’t really had it happen much in, say, an RV or a big truck, so I don’t want to pretend I’ve tested every kind of vehicle. Most of what I’m talking about is when I’m in a car and we’re coming up on one of those high bridges over the bay.

But I guess the important part is the vehicle being up there, if that makes sense. I know those bridges are built fine, and I know people go over them every day without anything happening. I can tell myself that. But when I get near one, my mind starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side. That’s the picture that comes into my head, and it feels real in the moment even though I know it’s not logical.
Is your fear of high bridges ever triggered by anything related to driving over them besides the act of driving itself?

Yeah… it’s not just the driving part, like the steering or traffic or anything like that. It’s really the moment I see the bridge coming up. As soon as I spot it ahead of me, even before I’m actually on it, I can feel my chest get tight, and my hands start sweating on the wheel.

Then I kind of lock in, if that makes sense. I start staring straight ahead, almost like if I look around too much it’ll make it worse, and I’m just thinking, “Just get to the other side.” It’s like my whole focus narrows down to making it across. So it’s related to driving over it, but the trigger is really seeing it coming up and knowing I’m about to have to go over it.
Is your fear of high bridges ever present when you are not in control of the vehicle, such as being a passenger in a taxi or ride-share crossing over a high bridge?

Yeah, I mean… if I’m not the one driving, it can still be there. It’s not only about me having my hands on the wheel. If we’re getting near one of those high bridges over the bay, my head still goes to that same place.

I know, logically, those bridges are built fine. I know people drive over them all day, every day, and nothing happens. I can say that sitting here and it sounds obvious. But when the car gets close to the bridge, whether I’m driving or just sitting there, my mind starts acting like the car could somehow go right over the side. It’s like that picture pops in there before I can stop it.

So in a taxi or ride-share, I think it would still bother me. Maybe in a different way because I’m not controlling the vehicle, but the fear is really about being in the car up on that bridge and having that thought that it could go over.
Do you ever feel this fear of going over the side when you're not in any kind of vehicle at all?

I don’t think so… not in the same way, anyway. I’m trying to think of a time when I was just standing somewhere, not in a car or anything, and felt that same “going over the side” fear, and nothing really comes to mind.

For me it seems tied to being on the bridge in a vehicle, or knowing I’m about to be. If I’m just walking around somewhere or looking at something high, I don’t think I get that same picture in my head. At least, I haven’t really noticed it. It’s more that whole situation of crossing over and being up there on the bridge.
